title: I made my first 3D game using AI
author: ineedthealgorithm
selftext:
I run a Pomodoro timer website called [Pomofox](https://www.pomofox.com/). Lately, many users have been asking the same thing: “Can we have a small game during break time?”

So I decided to try building one. I've created a 2D game with AI before, but not 3D. I wasn't familiar with the requirements, different asset types, etc. This felt like a good experiment.

The game is called **Pomofox: Shadow Break**. It’s a short 3D top-down action game. You play as a hooded fox and fight magical skeletons. The idea is to play for 1–2 minutes, then go back to work.

Here is the link to try: [https://www.pixelfork.ai/publish/0cdc7e1a-a957-4b76-9e61-b3e7ac2c6f1d](https://www.pixelfork.ai/publish/0cdc7e1a-a957-4b76-9e61-b3e7ac2c6f1d)

I created the game using **Three.js**.

This was my initial prompt:

>Create a 3D top-down action RPG using Three.js with a controllable character, enemies, and simple combat.

From there, I kept adding small changes:

* movement and combat
* enemies and waves
* pickups like health and shield
* loading screen and game over screen
* audios

I focused on keeping the scope small. Lots of small edits instead of big rewrites.

I found 3D assets from [Itch.io](http://Itch.io) (all GLB):

* Trees:[ https://venturon.itch.io/fir-trees-textured](https://venturon.itch.io/fir-trees-textured)
* Health & shield pickups:[ https://venturon.itch.io/health-magica-stamina-potions-3d-models-fbx-glb](https://venturon.itch.io/health-magica-stamina-potions-3d-models-fbx-glb)
* Skeleton enemies:[ https://brackeysgames.itch.io/brackeys-3d-game-tutorial-assets](https://brackeysgames.itch.io/brackeys-3d-game-tutorial-assets)
* Fox character:[ https://gtibo.itch.io/hooded-fox](https://gtibo.itch.io/hooded-fox)

The goal was not to make a big game. Just something simple that fits into a Pomodoro break.

Happy to answer questions about the process.
